answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation.. This holds because a newly minted alias starts worthless, so the attacker must first farm credibility on each one before it can swing a verdict. Consider a quill as the anchor of the cost.
